stem: A client is scheduled for a serum lipid panel whose laboratory profile specifies “Fasting (8 HR or more).” Which instruction is most accurate?

options.A: Eat a light meal two hours before collection because fasting does not affect the requested laboratory profile.
options.B: Follow the laboratory requirement and complete at least eight hours of fasting before the specimen is collected.
options.C: Fast for only one hour because longer fasting can invalidate the lipid measurements in this laboratory profile.
options.D: Automatically stop every prescribed morning medicine because all fasting lipid panels require withholding all medications.

rationale: Mayo Clinic Laboratories profile 616696 explicitly includes “Fasting (8 HR or more).” Therefore B directly follows the ordered laboratory requirement. A and C do not meet the specified fasting interval. D incorrectly turns a fasting instruction into a universal medication-withholding instruction; medication directions should follow the ordering clinician and laboratory-specific instructions.
educational_objective: Follow the exact patient-preparation requirement specified by the laboratory for a fasting lipid panel without adding unsupported medication restrictions.

source_original.stem: A client is scheduled for a serum lipid panel whose laboratory profile specifies “Fasting (8 HR or more).” Which instruction is most accurate?

options.A: Eat a light meal two hours before collection because fasting does not affect the requested laboratory profile.
options.B: Follow the laboratory requirement and complete at least eight hours of fasting before the specimen is collected.
options.C: Fast for only one hour because longer fasting can invalidate the lipid measurements in this laboratory profile.
options.D: Automatically stop every prescribed morning medicine because all fasting lipid panels require withholding all medications.

source_original.rationale: The cited Mayo Clinic Laboratories lipid-panel profile specifies fasting for 8 hours or more. Option B directly follows the laboratory's preparation requirement. Option A ignores the ordered fasting condition, Option C shortens it below the specified interval, and Option D incorrectly turns fasting into a universal instruction to stop prescribed medications; medication directions must follow individualized orders or laboratory instructions.
